purpose: Observe the placement and chaining of exactly zero, one, and two Jet 3 table-definition continuation pages under bounded empty first-create controls.

preregistration.prior_evidence: EXP-0059 records the bounded 18-byte physical-column record, one-byte CP1252 column-name length and bytes, definition logical-length field, 2,048-byte root capacity, and 2,040-byte continuation contribution. EXP-0061 records the bounded inline, single-page, and chained long-value framing used only to account for a created catalog LvProp value; EXP-0091 records null as a bounded consumable LvProp form. EXP-0073 records the bounded catalog, page-role, usage-map, and continuation-chain decoder. EXP-0087 and EXP-0093 record empty first-create framing and page roles for definitions that fit one page. EXP-0095 records that the first attempt reached capture_zero in all replicas but its combined 64-page geometry check retained no created arm and identified no failed clause. EXP-0059's separate wide-table endpoint referenced zero-based page index 172, implying a file of at least 173 pages; that is design input for choosing 256, the smallest power of two at least 173, as the completed-checkpoint bound, not evidence about these exact controls or the failed arm's size. The exact earlier boundary placement is design input only and does not establish where DAO places continuation pages in these controls.
preregistration.authorization: This successor is SHA-256-pinned and forbids acquisition until the exact preregistration commit is merged and the user makes a new explicit run decision because the EXP-0095 attempt reached a DAO mutation.
preregistration.attempt_policy: Dispatch at most one three-replica run after explicit authorization. Once the first DAO CreateDatabase mutation begins, any failure is a scientific result and must not be retried without another explicit human decision. A replica stops immediately after its first post-mutation failure.

execution.environment: The private local Windows development VM documented in docs/LOCAL_WINDOWS_VM.md, using x86 Windows PowerShell and a ready DAO.DBEngine.36 provider.
execution.independence: Each replica creates and closes one fresh dbVersion30 CP1252 database, retains it as empty, then copies and identity-checks it into three working arms before any TableDefs mutation. Each arm receives exactly one table append and is closed before metadata capture. No rows or indexes are added.

scenarios.zero: ContZero has 69 fixed dbLong fields with exact ten-byte ASCII names F000AAAAAA through F068AAAAAA. The recorded grammar gives a 2,046-byte logical definition, fitting the root with zero continuations.
scenarios.one: ContOneX has 70 otherwise identical fields F000AAAAAA through F069AAAAAA. The recorded grammar gives a 2,075-byte logical definition, requiring one continuation contribution.
scenarios.two: ContTwoX has 140 otherwise identical fields F000AAAAAA through F139AAAAAA. The recorded grammar gives a 4,105-byte logical definition, exceeding the root plus one 2,040-byte continuation contribution by 17 bytes and requiring a second continuation contribution.

execution.capture: All ephemeral bases and arms live under one newly created, non-reparse working subdirectory with at most twelve fixed working MDB names. Root publication is nonrecursive, so a working-file cleanup failure remains a producer failure without contaminating the exact retained root MDB inventory; no working artifact is published or interpreted. Before any table append, copy all three working arms in zero, one, two order and record an exact ordered arm_baselines entry after each copy passes its size, SHA-256, and measurement identity check against the retained empty image. A copy_arms failure may retain only the successfully checked ordered baseline prefix; phases at or after append_zero require all three entries, including a later failure during capture_zero. Before enforcing checkpoint policy, record the exact raw byte length, whether that length is divisible by 2,048, the derived page count when divisible, and the first failed predicate in fixed order: minimum_page_length, page_alignment, checkpoint_bound_exceeded. A completed checkpoint must be a regular non-reparse file of one through 256 pages. A passing producer retains exactly twelve closed MDB checkpoints with the same measurements, sizes, and SHA-256 values before and after bounded read-only DAO TableDefs metadata access. Capture the exact DAO table and field inventory, mutation_started, the bounded producer phase, and at most the active checkpoint's recovery image after a failure. failure_measurement may be present only for create_database after mutation starts, capture_empty, copy_arms, or an append/capture phase; it is null before CreateDatabase and for a cleanup-only failure at complete. Once CreateDatabase has set mutation_started, the active empty checkpoint may be recovered during create_database or capture_empty; later active scenario checkpoints may be recovered during their append or capture phases. An aligned active image above the 256-page checkpoint bound may be salvaged only through 512 pages with its exact size, SHA-256, measurement, reason checkpoint_bound_exceeded, and interpreted=false. Other bounded post-mutation recovery is likewise marked interpreted=false. Recovery bytes receive no DAO metadata access, are not decoded, and cannot answer any question. A failure above the recovery bound records its exact measurement but retains no MDB. For each completed arm, preserve all attributed appended LVAL pages and distinguish those referenced by the catalog LvProp from attributed but unreferenced nuisance allocation.

questions.continuation_counts: Do the 2,046-, 2,075-, and 4,105-byte definitions decode to exactly zero, one, and two continuation pages, respectively?
questions.placement: For each arm, where do the definition root and continuation pages land relative to the empty boundary; how does each chain pointer order them; what logical interval and used byte count does each page carry; and what recorded role and owner accounts for every appended page? No consecutive or relative page order is presumed.
questions.counters: What are the bounded page-0 counter values before and after each create, and how do their deltas correlate with the appended page count and catalog object identifier without assigning an unrecorded semantic?
questions.producer_outcome: Did all three replicas complete every exact arm?
questions.replication: Do the complete decoded relative observations agree across all three replicas?

decision_rule.accepted: The plan and all executed inputs match their final SHA-256 pins; all three replicas complete the exact four-checkpoint inventory once; every arm begins byte-identical to its retained empty image; every completed measurement is internally consistent, identifies no failed predicate, and records at most 256 pages; DAO metadata matches the exact declared schema; all retained bytes remain unchanged by metadata access; each definition has its exact preregistered logical length and decodes completely with the required zero, one, or two continuation pages; every appended page is attributed; the complete page-0 changed-offset set, counter, and catalog-root observations are present; and complete relative observations agree across replicas. A fully decoded nonconsecutive placement is an answered result.
decision_rule.no_outcome: Any post-mutation producer failure—including minimum-length, alignment, completed-checkpoint-bound, or recovery-bound failure—changed metadata identity, schema disagreement, decode or chain failure, unexpected logical length or continuation count, unattributed page, ambiguous counter/catalog correlation, incomplete later arm, or replica disagreement is recorded as no_outcome. A recovery-only image is never interpreted and cannot change that classification.
decision_rule.rejected: A pre-mutation plan, input, provider, or infrastructure failure; pin mismatch; malformed result or measurement; inconsistent mutation/phase/checkpoint/arm_baselines/recovery state; an arm_baselines entry that is out of order, exceeds three, differs from empty, or disagrees with its later checkpoint; unexpected, reordered, duplicate, missing, symlinked, or extra artifact; a completed checkpoint above 256 pages; a retained recovery above 512 pages; or analyzer contract defect rejects validation without a scientific outcome.
decision_rule.retry: There is no automatic retry after the first DAO mutation.

retention.publish: environment.json, result.json, the bounded job result, up to twelve exact expected-name MDBs including at most one explicitly identified, uninterpreted active-checkpoint recovery artifact per failed replica (exactly twelve completed checkpoints for a passing job), and the deterministic analyzer report. Completed checkpoints are at most 256 pages; recovery-only salvage is at most 512 pages.
retention.repository: Never commit MDB bytes or provider binaries. Record a validated report identity and conclusion once as a later additive EXP outcome.

publication.canonical_result: One validated deterministic JSON report and one later additive EXP outcome.

exclusions: definition chains longer than two continuation pages or tables above 140 columns
variable, Boolean, long-value, indexed, relationship, saved-query, or populated table definitions
general allocation policy, free-page reuse, or a presumption that continuation pages are consecutive

catalog LvProp payload grammar, a presumption that its storage remains single-page, or a claim that every attributed appended LVAL page must be referenced; only its raw header/reference and referenced versus unreferenced LVAL inventory may be preserved
names above ASCII 0x7E, names of other lengths, and locale or collation behavior
public creation API, initial rows, filesystem publication, writer correctness, hosted differential #102, compatibility claims, and support-matrix movement
